history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: Deulghata Temples = seq 1186 (id deulghat-temple-deulghata). HERITAGE FLAG: Deulghata is an archaeological cluster of ancient temples in ruins, taken over by the Archaeological Survey of India; it is a heritage monument, NOT a functioning temple (keep/drop decision for the user). Once 15 temples and small shrines on the bank of the Kangsabati, ~6 km south of Jaypur and ~25 km from Purulia town. Dating is disputed: the District Census Handbook/Wikipedia place them in the 9th-10th century (Pala era), while other sources attribute them to the 11th-12th century Sena period (flag: verify). Three tall brick rekha deuls with Pala-Sena-age stucco decoration (chaitya motifs, geese scrollwork, dwarfs) survive; the stone temples have fallen. E.T. Dalton found the three large temples amid ruins in 1864-65; J.D. Beglar of the ASI reported them in 1872-73. Ganesh and Durga images have been found at the site; stone idols are stored in a nearby temple. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Purulia' is the district; the site is near Boram in the Arsha block, ~25 km from Purulia town.

name: Deulghata Temples
town_description: Deulghata (also Deulghat) is a rural site in the Arsha block of Purulia district, on the bank of the Kangsabati river, known for its cluster of ancient Pala/Sena-era brick temples in ruins.

travel.road: Near Boram village, Arsha block, ~6 km south of Jaypur and ~25 km from Purulia town; last stretch is a rural road (verify)
